analysis_claims.universe: Endpoint-specific valid baseline/follow-up pairs among returners, retaining original assignment. Eligible bases include everyone enrolled in each arm. Missing counts describe each enrolled arm at each wave; they can overlap and cannot be summed to obtain unique pair exclusions.
analysis_claims.weighting: Fixed weight_base; both waves use the same endpoint-specific paired weights. Rounded supplied-table transcriptions, not new raw-data estimates.

analysis_claims.universe: Separate valid-case distributions at each wave, pooled across assignment. Baseline eligibility is all enrolled; follow-up eligibility is returned questionnaires. These are not paired changes or a conversion funnel.
analysis_claims.weighting: Fixed weight_base; each distribution uses its own valid-case denominator. Rounded supplied-table transcriptions.

analysis_claims.universe: Endpoint-specific observed pairs in four disjoint assignment-by-children cells. Interaction is the children assignment contrast minus the no-children assignment contrast.
analysis_claims.weighting: Fixed weight_base; supplied paired-change inference. Intervals are pointwise. Holm adjustment applies to the three interaction tests, not subgroup-specific contrasts.

findings.proposition: Assignment to BasketBridge invitations produced a supported positive awareness contrast among observed pairs: awareness increased from 30.83% to 58.76% in the assigned arm (+27.93 percentage points), versus 31.37% to 45.70% in control (+14.33 points). The difference in change was +13.59 points.
findings.claim_strength: Positive observed-pair assignment contrast, significant after primary-family Holm adjustment.
findings.qualification: SE 2.077 points; pointwise 95% CI 9.52 to 17.66; raw p=6.032e-11, Holm p=1.810e-10. Control/assigned valid paired bases (unweighted N, weighted N, Kish ESS): (1016,999.79,876.62)/(960,965.21,834.41); eligible bases: (1400,1387.06,1210.61)/(1400,1412.94,1220.30). Selection into observed pairs prevents an unqualified full-cohort causal claim. Control growth cannot be attributed to a particular mechanism. Full primary distributions and missingness appear in PRIMARY_PAIRED_DISTRIBUTIONS.

findings.proposition: Neither consideration nor reported use demonstrated incremental benefit. Top-two consideration increased from 28.68% to 37.04% under assignment (+8.36 points), versus 31.49% to 39.86% in control (+8.36): a -0.008-point contrast. Reported use increased from 6.19% to 8.80% under assignment (+2.61), versus 5.51% to 9.10% in control (+3.59): a -0.98-point contrast.
findings.claim_strength: No detected assignment difference in either downstream outcome; equivalence and harm are unestablished.
findings.qualification: Consideration: SE 1.750 points, pointwise 95% CI -3.44 to 3.42, raw/Holm p=.9962; control/assigned paired bases (N, weighted N, Kish ESS)=(1015,1000.17,877.62)/(966,973.61,839.32). Usage: SE .877, CI -2.70 to .74, raw p=.2641, Holm p=.5281; paired bases=(1007,993.81,868.83)/(969,973.30,842.04). Eligible bases for both endpoints: control (1400,1387.06,1210.61), assigned (1400,1412.94,1220.30). Full distributions and missingness appear in PRIMARY_PAIRED_DISTRIBUTIONS. Consideration followed the identical neutral description for everyone at both waves. Use is self-reported over nonoverlapping four-week windows, not verified activity, transactions or sales.

findings.proposition: Selective follow-up limits generalisation. Control returned 1,070 questionnaires and assignment 1,019, with weighted return rates of 75.98% and 72.38%. Returners had higher baseline consideration and lower budget pressure than nonreturners.
findings.claim_strength: Descriptive evidence of selection; outcome-bias direction and magnitude remain unknown.
findings.qualification: Return-rate eligible=valid bases (N, weighted N, Kish ESS), control/assigned: (1400,1387.06,1210.61)/(1400,1412.94,1220.30), with no missingness or structural exclusions. Nonreturner/returner baseline eligible bases: (711,723.48,622.07)/(2089,2076.52,1808.85). Baseline top-two consideration: 21.99%/30.13%; valid bases (691,704.14,604.75)/(2028,2018.38,1756.82), missing 97/98/99=(9,3,8)/(36,13,12). High/very-high budget pressure: 49.20%/33.68%; valid bases (692,703.06,605.98)/(2036,2026.36,1762.90), missing=(12,2,5)/(34,11,8). Baseline structural exclusions are zero. Endpoint-specific pair exclusions appear in PRIMARY_PAIRED_DISTRIBUTIONS. Fixed baseline weights do not correct attrition.

findings.proposition: Receipt and recall associations cannot substitute for the assignment result. Logged receipt was 70.16% under assignment and 24.54% in control, so the study tests invitations with incomplete receipt and crossover. Recipients' follow-up consideration advantage was 19.12 points against a pre-existing 19.15-point baseline advantage; recallers' follow-up advantage was 37.24 points against 32.35 points at baseline.
findings.claim_strength: Descriptive implementation and observational associations; no causal receipt or recall effect.
findings.qualification: Receipt-rate eligible=valid bases (N, weighted N, Kish ESS), assigned/control: (1400,1412.94,1220.30)/(1400,1387.06,1210.61), with no missingness or structural exclusions. For consideration comparisons, receipt=0/1 eligible=valid paired bases: (944,1003.75,820.43)/(1037,970.04,903.73), total 1981, no grouping exclusions. Recall=0/1 eligible=valid subgroup bases: (1040,1107.13,906.03)/(844,760.65,741.87); 97 of the 1981 consideration pairs lack valid recall and are excluded, with no code-specific split supplied. Outcomes have no remaining missingness within these preselected pairs. Each grouping compares the same people at both waves. Receipt is not proven attention; recall was measured after outcomes. Neither grouping was randomised, and neither identifies mediation or an effect among compliers.

findings.proposition: Households with children have greater reported meal-planning stress, but superior campaign response is unestablished. Very/extremely stressful planning was reported by 56.48% with children versus 36.56% without. The priority audience's assignment contrasts were +10.15 points for awareness, +2.95 for consideration and +0.91 for use; no children-versus-no-children interaction passed Holm adjustment.
findings.claim_strength: Descriptive audience need; no detected prespecified response heterogeneity.
findings.qualification: Stress eligible bases (N, weighted N, Kish ESS), children/no children: (1090,979.51,985.73)/(1710,1820.49,1471.74); valid bases (1060,950.38,958.69)/(1686,1791.67,1451.12); missing 97/98/99=(16,6,8)/(17,4,3); structural exclusions=0. Children-specific pointwise 95% CIs: awareness 3.52 to 16.79; consideration -2.90 to 8.80; use -2.30 to 4.12. Children-minus-no-children interactions: awareness -5.07 (CI -13.46 to 3.32; raw p=.2358, Holm .4717), consideration +4.27 (CI -2.95 to 11.48; raw .2464, Holm .4717), use +2.81 (CI -.98 to 6.59; raw .1459, Holm .4378). Four-cell eligible/valid bases, missingness, arm changes and interaction SEs appear in CHILDREN_ASSIGNMENT_RESULTS. Subgroup intervals do not inherit interaction-family multiplicity control. Need can motivate a children-focused test; effectiveness-based preferential targeting is not established.

findings.proposition: Message ratings offer creative-testing hypotheses: among recorded recallers, agreement was 76.74% for clarity, 70.52% for relevance and 75.90% for believability. Relevance's lower numerical rating does not establish it as the weakest attribute or explain the awareness result.
findings.claim_strength: Selected-recaller descriptive diagnostics; no tested ranking or causal-driver inference.
findings.qualification: All items have eligible base (N, weighted N, Kish ESS)=(891,800.64,781.76), with 1909 structural exclusions. Clarity/relevance/believability valid bases: (862,773.02,755.96)/(854,770.28,747.66)/(852,765.17,749.26); missing 97/98/99=(22,3,4)/(25,6,6)/(33,3,3). Full distributions from strongly disagree through strongly agree: clarity [0.47,3.62,19.17,30.88,45.86]%; relevance [2.06,8.58,18.84,27.02,43.49]%; believability [1.39,6.73,15.97,29.27,46.63]%. The selected route and different valid bases limit comparisons. These ratings do not establish what would improve downstream behaviour.

findings.proposition: Recommend a further controlled test with better outcome recovery and a prespecified meaningful downstream objective. The awareness result supports further testing; these data do not establish a commercial-return case for wider rollout.
findings.claim_strength: Researcher recommendation synthesising assignment results and follow-up limitations.
findings.qualification: This is a decision recommendation, not a new empirical estimate or proof that another campaign will succeed. Supporting estimates, uncertainty and bases are in F1, F2 and F4. Priority-audience need and message diagnostics can inform hypotheses, but neither establishes superior targeting or a causal improvement lever. Costs, revenue and actual sales were not measured, so ROI cannot be estimated.

beats.headline_intent: Invitations increased awareness growth among observed pairs, without demonstrated downstream benefit.
beats.analytical_relationship: Compare assigned and control paired changes separately for each endpoint, retaining primary-family Holm inference and pointwise uncertainty.

beats.headline_intent: Selective follow-up limits the scope of that conclusion.
beats.analytical_relationship: Qualify the observed-pair findings using return rates, baseline selection and endpoint-specific completeness; do not extend them to the full randomised cohort.

beats.headline_intent: Receipt and recall associations do not provide an alternative effectiveness claim.
beats.analytical_relationship: Explain the invitation-policy estimand through incomplete receipt and crossover, then contrast observational follow-up differences with pre-existing baseline differences.

beats.headline_intent: Audience need and message ratings inform hypotheses, without proving superior targeting or creative choices.
beats.analytical_relationship: Separate descriptive audience need from tested response heterogeneity, and selected-recaller ratings from attribute superiority or causal drivers.

beats.headline_intent: Use a better-recovered controlled test to establish meaningful downstream benefit before claiming commercial returns.
beats.analytical_relationship: Translate the supported awareness contrast, unresolved downstream outcomes and selection limits into a bounded research recommendation.

method_notes: Only the four supplied files reproduced in the prompt were used. No tools, browsing, connectors, other files or delegated agents were used. No new raw-data analysis was performed; analysis_claims contain rounded supplied-table transcriptions.
The service, participants and target profile are fictional. The eligible online-recontact panel is not a national probability sample; these estimates do not describe real UK prevalence.

Primary estimates preserve original random assignment, including noncompliers, and use each endpoint's own valid baseline/follow-up pairs. Both wave levels use the same paired base. This is assignment-based change among observed pairs, not full-cohort ITT with all randomised outcomes recovered.

Consideration codes 4–5 define top-two; valid codes 1–3 contribute zero. Codes 97/98/99 and structural blanks are excluded, never imputed as No or zero. Separate wave-valid and paired distributions, including all five consideration categories, are retained in analysis_claims. Different denominators must not be combined into a conversion funnel.

All reported estimates use fixed weight_base, based on baseline age-by-online-grocery profile. Weighted N is a sum of weights, not population size. Kish ESS diagnoses weight concentration; it does not replace paired-change variance or correct attrition.

Inference uses the supplied independent-household fixed-weight normal approximation. For paired change D, each arm variance is n/(n-1) times sum[w²(D−weighted mean D)²]/(sum w)². Assignment-contrast variance adds arm variances; interaction variance adds four disjoint-cell variances. No retained primary or interaction estimate has degenerate zero variance.

Intervals are pointwise 95%, not simultaneous. Holm adjustment controls each declared three-test family separately at .05; it does not jointly control both families, subgroup-specific tests or exploratory comparisons. Numerical ordering is not proof of superiority; nonsignificance is not evidence of zero effect or equivalence.

Numeric missingness and structural exclusions are separate. Wave-specific missing counts can overlap and cannot be added to infer unique pair losses. Rounded distributions may not sum exactly to 100. Unreported code-specific grouping exclusions have not been invented.

The exploratory older digital online-grocery subgroup has only 22 control and 21 assigned awareness pairs: insufficient base under the declared suppression rule, per analysis_results.json#/tables/older_digital_online/values/arms. No percentages, contrasts, intervals, p-values or targeting recommendation are reported for it.

Fixed-weight inference omits nonresponse-selection and target-profile uncertainty. The study does not establish full-cohort or whole-population effects, causal receipt effects, mediation, actual-sales impact or ROI. Recommendations remain distinct from demonstrated outcomes.
